title: Migrate plugins/agent/monitor to contract v2
goal: Move the monitor plugin's result, disposition, budgets, and inputs onto contract v2 (#1821-#1826, #1829) while keeping the live deployed.yaml dispatch behavior-identical for a passing run

steps.description: Declare v2 metadata in the manifest: provides.result_contract: 2; config.router: {timeout_s: 300, max_turns: 10} (Pattern-1 single-shot headroom, mirrors review-lens/manifest.yaml); a one-line comment recording that no release/cleanup hook is declared because monitor holds no live resources (ADR-001 'absence is recorded, not implied' - the engine's plugin.cleanup.absent event covers this automatically). valid_verdicts (pass,degraded), the primary:true monitor_report output, provides.role, and provides.events are already present - leave them.

Test-first: extend monitor-test.sh with failing SPECs before touching plugin.sh - assert .result_contract==2 and .disposition=="complete" on the existing dry-run/live-pass paths (SPEC-2/3), .disposition mapped via router_reason_disposition on model error (SPEC-4), a new SPEC for SIGTERM/SIGINT during the model call writing disposition:"interrupted", and a new SPEC for router rc=10 (turn-budget exhaustion) writing disposition:"out_of_turns" - not "exhausted", which core/pipeline/disposition.sh documents as retired by #2187 (the issue's ADR-063 §3 citation of disposition:exhausted / disposition.sh:97->escalate is stale against current code). Run and confirm each new/changed assertion fails for the right reason before step-3.

Replace _monitor_write_report with a v2 result writer (_monitor_write_result), mirroring _review_lens_write_result/_design_write_result: emit {result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason, data:{summary, checks}} - folding today's rendered summary/checks strings into the namespaced data block per the issue's 'Folds in' section, atomic_write as before.

Source scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh and wire disposition on every exit path of _monitor_stage_run_inner: dry-run and healthy-model paths -> "complete"; route_to_model rc!=0 -> router_reason_disposition(classified reason); unparseable/schema-gate-failed envelope -> "unusable"; degraded verdict from a well-formed response -> "complete" (the stage ran fine, the verdict itself says degraded). Every rc/verdict combination already exercised by SPEC-2..4 must still pass.

Add a SIGTERM/SIGINT trap (mirrors _review_lens_interrupt_handler) around the route_to_model call that writes disposition:"interrupted" and, separately, an explicit branch for router rc==10 that writes disposition:"out_of_turns" reason:"budget_exhausted" and returns 10 so the engine's existing +50%-capped-at-2x escalation (route.sh's out_of_turns retry path) actually gets exercised for monitor, which the issue's Refs section says has never happened for this stage.

Add ADR-063 §1 budget guidance (_monitor_budget_guidance, _monitor_wallclock_guidance, modeled on review-lens's equivalents) sourced from _route_resolve_max_turns/_route_resolve_timeout, appended to the prompt before the route_to_model call so the model is told its actual turn/timeout limits from the manifest's step-1 router block rather than a hand-copied literal.

Delete the hardcoded deploy_result_json/pr_url_txt path construction in favor of reading them from $ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS (engine-resolved name-matched inputs, #1825/#1826), matching design_stage_run's read-then-fallback pattern so existing fixtures without ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS set keep working.

Extend the deployed.yaml e2e test's SPEC-9 (behavior-unchanged golden check) to assert the new v2 fields (result_contract:2, disposition:"complete") are present on a passing dry-run alongside the pre-existing verdict/monitor-report.json assertions, giving the before/after golden diff the acceptance checklist requires. A tests/ grep for monitor-report.json|monitor_stage_run|monitor-summary.md found no other pinned files, so this plus monitor-test.sh (step-2) is the complete test-scope.

notes: monitor was already fully dispatched in config/templates/deployed.yaml before this issue (pr->deploy->validate->monitor, verified via SPEC-2/5/9 in deployed-template-e2e-test.sh) and its manifest already had valid_verdicts, a primary:true output, provides.role, and provides.events - the issue's own acceptance checklist anticipates this ('if this plugin already declares one, say so and move on'), so steps 1/8 are additive, not remedial. The bigger finding: the issue's 'ALSO LAND HERE' section directs writing disposition:"exhausted" and cites disposition.sh:97 mapping it to an 'escalate' response driven by route.sh:749's +50%-capped-at-2x retry. Reading core/pipeline/disposition.sh as it exists on this branch shows "exhausted" was retired by #2187 precisely because it mapped to an unimplemented 'escalate' action and hid which budget (turns vs wall-clock) ran out; the current closed set uses "out_of_turns" for turn exhaustion and "timed_out" for wall-clock, both already routed to a 'retry' response, and scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh's router_reason_disposition confirms router_out_of_turns maps to out_of_turns. review-lens/plugin.sh already implements exactly this rc==10 -> disposition:"out_of_turns" pattern working end-to-end. This plan follows the current, working vocabulary (out_of_turns) rather than the issue's stale 'exhausted' citation; a human should confirm that's the intended correction before merge, since it's a direct deviation from the literal issue text even though it's required by the anti-drift rule (spec/code wins over a stale issue comment). Assumption: manifest config.router values of timeout_s:300/max_turns:10 are proposed by analogy to review-lens's identical Pattern-1 comment ('single-shot advisory; no exploration loop needed' / 'headroom for retry on schema failure') - not independently derived from monitor-specific load data, since none was available to read in this planning pass. Cleanup/release hook: no plugin.sh code changes planned since monitor holds no live resources; step-1's manifest comment plus the engine's existing plugin.cleanup.absent auto-emit is treated as satisfying that acceptance line, but this is a judgment call worth a reviewer's sign-off rather than a hook stub with nothing to release.
